## 2026-10-13: ETSI TR 103 562 self-announcement arm (branch sensys/etsi-self-announcement)

ARM. `LateFusionEtsiSelfAnnouncementEdge` (ecav/core/application/edge/edge_manager/edge_manager_late_fusion_etsi_self_announcement_ab3dmot_linear_predictor.py), registry keys `LATE_FUSION_ETSI_SELF_ANNOUNCEMENT` and `ETSI_SELF_ANNOUNCEMENT`. It is the state-of-the-art baseline against self-beacon anchoring: ETSI TR 103 562 V2.1.1 section 4.5.6 lets a station omit from its CPM any perceived object it matched to a received CAM, assuming every receiver holds the CAM. The rule lives at the SENDER. Every CAV and every RSU matches its detections to the beacons it can see (never its own) by a greedy one-to-one nearest-displacement match inside a speed-scaled gate, gate = max(etsi_match_min_gate_m, etsi_match_tolerance * beacon speed * beacon age), the BeaconIdManager reconciliation gate floored at 5 m, and omits the matched detections from its uplink before the payload is built. The edge then runs the plain late-fusion AB3DMOT merge with `anchoring` forced off (a warning if the yaml says true); beacons still reach the edge as rows exactly as in the no-contract late-fusion arm. Self-beacon anchoring code is untouched. The base class gained one hook, `PredictionLateFusionEdge._sender_payload(sender_tag, sender_vid, src_objects, beacons, frame_idx)`, identity by default; `update_information` now collects beacons for all MAC-delivered vehicles before any object list is built, so the per-vehicle MAC loss still drops a vehicle's beacon and objects together and the default arm's packets are unchanged. RSU senders are tagged `rsu_<rid>` (the RSUManager attribute is `rid`, not `id`; the old tag collapsed both RSUs into `rsu_rsu`).

BEACON VISIBILITY AT SENDERS. The simulator delivers beacons only to the edge (`beacons[vid] = (location, extent)` in `update_information`); no CAV-to-CAV or CAV-to-RSU broadcast exists. The arm therefore records each tick's delivered beacon set, with velocity from the vehicle manager, into a bounded history (`_record_broadcast`) and lets each sender use the newest beacon per vehicle whose age lies in [etsi_beacon_delay_ticks, etsi_beacon_delay_ticks + etsi_beacon_max_age_ticks], propagated to the current tick under constant velocity (`_visible_beacons`). Defaults delay 0, max age 2 ticks: a zero-delay broadcast at the beacon cadence, the most favourable case for the rule. A sender's own beacon is never visible to it. The delay and max-age knobs are the fault-injection handles for the receiver-missed-the-message case; the MAC model's per-vehicle uplink loss already removes a vehicle's beacon for everyone in that tick.

COUNTERS (logged per tick as `[ETSI] tick= sender= omitted= true_self= other_actor= no_gt= missed_self(no_beacon= gate=) kept= visible_beacons=`, totals and per-sender in `simulation_metrics.json` under `edges.<id>.etsi_self_announcement`). Each omitted detection is judged against the per-tick CARLA snapshot already taken by `update_information` (nearest actor within etsi_gt_match_radius_m = 2.5 m): `omitted_true_self` (the detection sits on the beaconing vehicle it matched), `omitted_other_actor` (it sits on a different vehicle: the ETSI wrong-match failure, a real object dropped; each one also logs `[ETSI-WRONG]` with the beacon vid, displacement to the beacon, beacon age, the GT actor id, type and displacement), `omitted_no_gt` (no vehicle within the radius: a false positive or a badly localised self detection; nothing real lost). Kept detections of another managed CAV count as `missed_self_no_beacon` (the sender held no usable beacon) or `missed_self_gate` (a beacon was visible but the gate rejected the match): the ETSI missed-message failure. Derived: `omitted_wrong_fraction`, `omitted_no_gt_fraction`, `self_announced_forwarded_fraction`.

CONFIG. ecav/scenario_testing/config_yaml/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_etsi_smoke.yaml (copy of openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_smoke.yaml: 2 RSUs + 1 CAV, YOLO on localhost:18001, Scenario_3 town03, seed 11) with `manager_type: late_fusion_etsi_self_announcement`, `anchoring: false`, `etsi_match_min_gate_m: 5.0`, `etsi_match_tolerance: 1.5`, `etsi_beacon_delay_ticks: 0`, `etsi_beacon_max_age_ticks: 2`, `etsi_gt_match_radius_m: 2.5`; scenario file ecav/scenario_testing/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_etsi_smoke.py delegates to openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion. start_actors.sh now treats any manager type containing `late_fusion` as late fusion (YOLO server auto-start); its default CONDA_ENV ecav310 does not exist here and it wipes every docker container and pkills CARLA, so the smokes ran the sequential path by hand (CARLA 0.9.15 headless, ecav/ml_manager/yolo_grpc_server.py on 18001, test_runner.py).

ONE-SEED COMMAND (opencda310, from the repo root, CARLA on 2000 and the YOLO gRPC server on 18001 up):
`/home/atlas/anaconda3/envs/opencda310/bin/python test_runner.py -t openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_etsi_smoke --latencies 100 --repetitions 1`
Results under experiment_results/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_etsi_smoke/<STAMP>/.../run_1/simulation_metrics.json. The other arms take `--manager-types` on the shared yaml; this arm has its own yaml because its edge block carries the etsi_* keys.

WORKTREE PROVISIONING (not committed). A fresh worktree lacks the gitignored protobuf stubs and the submodule checkouts. Stubs: `python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I./ecav/protos --python_out=./ecav/protos --grpc_python_out=./ecav/protos ecav/protos/{ecloud,perception,migration}.proto` with the env's protoc (protobuf 6.31.1; the main checkout's stubs fail to import with "Couldn't parse file content" and lack perception_pb2_grpc). Submodules scenario_runner, sort and ecav/worldfusion were symlinked from the main checkout (git shows them as type changes; never stage them). The YOLO server needs ./yolov5 in the worktree.

SMOKE (one seed, latency 100 ms, seed 11, commit 7eacddef, fresh CARLA 0.9.15 on port 2000 with no other client attached; three earlier attempts on the shared instance were invalidated by a sibling track's client resetting the world mid-run and by CUDA out-of-memory with two CARLA servers plus four YOLO servers on the 16 GB GPU). ETSI arm (experiment_results/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_etsi_smoke/20261013_201434): runner wall 120 s, edge 103.9 s, s_op 1 (coll 1, ghost 1, fp 1, prog 1), focal mean speed 8.93 m/s, 0 brake events, MAC 300/300 beacon ticks delivered, detections tp 524 / fp 1918 / fn 387, 0 ego ghost tracks, 0 geometric duplicate tracks, 0 spatial self-id failures. Sender rule: 330 omitted of 5184 detections (152 true self, 111 other actor, 67 no GT), 0 missed self (every self detection the RSUs made while a beacon was visible was omitted), omitted_wrong_fraction 0.336, omitted_no_gt_fraction 0.203. The CAV omitted nothing: with one CAV there is no other beacon for it to see, so in this scenario the rule acts only at the RSUs. rsu2 (-40,140): 108 omitted, 100 true self, 8 other actor. rsu1 (-82,128): 222 omitted, 52 true self, 103 other actor, 67 no GT. The 111 wrong matches are the ETSI wrong-match failure made measurable: 99 sit at 3.5 to 5 m from the beacon (inside the 5 m floor only) and the GT actor under them is the adjacent-lane column Scenario_3 spawns 3.8 m beside the ego's path (patrol 230 at 0.8 m, coupe 228 at 2.2 m, a2 226 at 1.5 m, model3 227 at 2.1 m from the detection): rsu1 detects the neighbour, the ego's own detection is absent or farther from the beacon, and the greedy one-to-one match hands the beacon to the neighbour, which is then dropped from the uplink. The gate floor (etsi_match_min_gate_m) is the knob that trades these against missed self omissions; a floor sweep is the parent's call, not run here.
Baseline late fusion, same instance, run right after (experiment_results/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_smoke/20261013_201643): runner wall 73 s, edge 57.9 s, s_coll 1, s_ghost 1, s_fp 1, s_prog 0 (focal mean speed 3.10 m/s against the 60 percent of target threshold), s_op 0, 2 brake events (neither ghost nor other false positive), MAC 300/300, detections tp 487 / fp 1897 / fn 490, 0 ego ghost tracks, 9 geometric duplicate tracks, 0 spatial self-id failures. An earlier baseline on the first shared instance with no other client attached (20261013_194848) gave s_prog 0 at 6.06 m/s, 0 brake events, 16 geometric duplicate tracks, 300/300 beacons. Both arms run end to end through the reproduce path; one seed says nothing about their relative safety outcome. The runner's per-run wall time is 70 to 120 s for 300 edge frames, so a 20-rep cell is about 30 min on this machine with the GPU to itself.

SHARED-HOST HAZARDS SEEN TODAY. test_runner.py hardcodes CARLA port 2000 and attaches to whatever listens there; two tracks running smokes at once share one world and each scenario_runner start resets the other's run (symptoms: spawn-tick sim_t far above the 2.8 to 3.4 s of a clean start, MAC total_attempted below 300, edge duration 15 s, focal speed 0). A client killed mid-scenario leaves the world dirty and the next Scenario_3 fails to spawn the Tesla. Each ecav.py client also loads YOLO in-process (about 550 MiB) on top of the gRPC server, and two CARLA servers hold 2.5 to 7 GB each, so the 16 GB GPU runs out with two tracks active. Serialize smokes across tracks or give each track its own CARLA port by patching the yaml's client_port and scenario_runner.port.

## 2026-10-13: per-tick age-at-use logging, reduction script, ns-3 payload fact (branch sensys/per-tick-age-logging)

Worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-a7c8f014855cd9bef`, branch `sensys/per-tick-age-logging` off develop 3fe4e0da. Commits c6002ae3 (logger, base wiring, smoke yaml knob, runner flag, reduction), d44b1bd6 (reduction: edge silence), cea65cce (reduction: conflict-brake age), 90c77656 (publish-sequence fix). Reviewer items A4/C4 (per-object age at use, conflict-time age, critical-object age, burst loss) and C7 (ns-3 payload sizes, Table 2 arithmetic).

PER-TICK AGE LOGGER (`ecav/core/application/edge/per_tick_age_logger.py`). Writes `per_tick_age.csv` into run_output_dir beside simulation_metrics.json, so the test_runner copies it into `run_N/evaluation_output/`. Off by default; one YAML knob in the edge block, `per_tick_age_log: {enabled: true, match_radius_m: 5.0}` (conflict_xy and cross_traffic_type default from the conflict_kinematics block). test_runner flag `--per-tick-age-log` turns the knob on for every edge and records `config_per_tick_age_log: true` in the metrics. Hook: `_BaseEdgeManager._record_time_to_events(tick, vm)`, which late-fusion, oracle and VIPS all call once per managed vehicle per tick after the planner step, so no subclass changes. One row per (tick, focal vehicle, consumed prediction) over `agent.generated_predictions` (the planner's edge cache merged with local predictions), plus one blank-object row with source `none` when nothing was consumed. Columns: tick, sim_time_s, wall_time_s, focal_vehicle_id, track_id, carla_id, source (edge/local/none), provenance (self = carla_id is the focal vehicle; anchored = real actor id with anchoring on; identified = real id with anchoring off; anonymous = -1 or guid > 10000, the planner's own rule), gen_tick (the prediction's source_tick), publish_tick, publish_seq (edge publish sequence number), consume_tick, age_at_use_ms = (consume - gen) x dt, publish_age_ms, obs_x, obs_y, obs_speed_mps, conflict_actor_id, is_conflict_actor (GT conflict actor by id, or an anonymous track within match_radius_m of that actor's live pose; the actor is picked as ConflictKinematicsLogger picks it: moving vehicle of cross_traffic_type nearest conflict_xy), conflict_dist_m, ego_speed_mps, ctrl_throttle, ctrl_brake, decision (brake if ctrl.brake >= 0.5, yield if > 0, else go), brake_event (a new brake_attributions entry this tick), brake_reason (ghost_reason), gt_brake_class, ttc_s. No boxes, no trajectories. Size on the smoke: 617 KB for 239 ticks (about 18 consumed objects per tick because the planner's edge cache holds entries for 24 ticks); a 1200-tick matrix run would be about 3 MB.

PUBLISH SEQUENCE FIX (90c77656). The first knob-on smoke had publish_seq blank on every row: the base constructor wrapped `self.lin_pred.generate_predicted_trajectories`, but the late-fusion (`:299`), oracle (`:148`) and VIPS (`:243`) managers each assign a new `self.lin_pred` after `super().__init__`, so the wrapper was lost in every SenSys manager. `lin_pred` is now a property on the base; its setter wraps whatever predictor is assigned (marker `_ptage_wrapped`, idempotent, no-op when the logger is off), so the numbering survives subclass reassignment. Offline check (scratch wrap_test): subclass reassignment numbered, empty publish not numbered, positional publish_tick not numbered, re-wrap idempotent. Live check: the final smoke has publish_seq on all 4325 edge rows, 237 distinct publishes consumed, sequence 0..236 with no gap.

REDUCTION (`safety_envelope_paper/reduce_per_tick_age.py`; the directory is gitignored, add with `git add -f`). Usage: `python safety_envelope_paper/reduce_per_tick_age.py RUN_OR_CAMPAIGN_DIR [...] [--out summary.csv] [--json summary.json] [--boot 2000] [--ci 0.95] [--focal lowest|all]`. Finds per_tick_age.csv in a run dir or its evaluation_output/, walks campaign dirs, groups runs by path with run_N / __run_N removed (test_runner layout and SenSys archive layout). Per run: global_p99_age_ms (edge rows), critical_object_p99_ms (is_conflict_actor rows), conflict_time_age_ms (the conflict actor's age at the first brake tick; NaN when the actor was not in the consumed set at that tick), conflict_brake_age_ms (age at the first brake tick where the actor was consumed), edge_silence_max_ticks, burst_loss_max and missed_publish_frac over publish_seq gaps, p50/p95. Per group: mean, median and bootstrap percentile CI over runs (seeds). Checked on synthetic two-run data and on the smoke.

SMOKE (openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_smoke through test_runner, opencda310, YOLO gRPC on 18001). Worktree assets missing as empty submodule dirs, symlinked from the main checkout and not committed: scenario_runner, sort, ecav/worldfusion, data; protobuf stubs regenerated with grpc_tools. Three completed runs under experiment_results/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion_smoke/: verbatim 20261013_195358 (knob off: no per_tick_age.csv, RET -6 = the pre-existing interpreter abort at exit from the 2026-09-14 entry, metrics written; edge 300 frames in 485 s at 1365 ms/frame under GPU contention, focal vehicle 642 stuck from the start on anonymous tracks 4 m from ego: 2 ghost brakes by proximity, 1 collision, 1.2 m travelled); knob on before the fix 20261013_200437 (RET 0, 300 frames in 125 s, focal 1102 no ghost brake, no collision, 33.6 m; publish_seq blank); knob on with the fix 20261013_201850 on a fresh CARLA (RET 0, 300 frames in 60 s at 185 ms/frame, focal 109 no ghost brake, no collision, 28.9 m). Final CSV: 4327 rows over 239 ticks, all edge rows anonymous (anchoring is off in this smoke), age at use p50 50 ms / p95 1350 / p99 1550 / max 1750 ms (the 24-tick edge cache hold plus source lag; publish age p50 is 0 ms, so a fresh publish is consumed on arrival and the tail is held entries), critical-object p99 334 ms over 133 proximity-matched conflict rows, conflict_time_age NaN (first brake at tick 26 had no conflict-actor row), conflict_brake_age 50 ms at tick 35, burst loss 0 and missed 0 (no loss configured), edge silence max 2 ticks. The verbatim and knob-on outcomes differ because the smoke is not deterministic under contention (edge frame time 1365 vs 399 vs 185 ms; the KB already records unseeded decision-arrival jitter); the logger only reads planner state and the predictor wrapper is transparent. Two further launches collided with a peer's ETSI smoke attached to the same CARLA on port 2000 (two clients in one world reset each other's scenario; "parent actor not found"); those attempts were discarded and the launches serialised by message with the peer.

NS-3 PAYLOAD AND TABLE 2 (reviewer C7; full write-up with file:line evidence in the paper repo, `reviews/ns3_payload_and_table2.md`, commit ba5515f, not pushed). Table 2's KB/s column was computed as p95 x 20 Hz / 1024 (KiB) from a 413 B average and 472 B p95 object list (beacon 96 x 20 / 1024 = 1.875 -> 1.88; list 413 x 20 / 1024 = 8.066 -> 8.06; total 9.94 exact), so the printed 4,130 / 4,720 B carry an extra digit; the wire layout caps the list at 4 + 4 + 10 x 48 + 4 = 492 B and the late-fusion manager's constants say "~430 B". Corrected row: 413 / 472 B, 8.07 KiB/s (p95 9.22), total 9.94 KiB/s (p95 11.1); in decimal kB/s 1.92 / 8.26 / 10.2. The ns-3 LUT (`data/ns3_uplink_lut.csv`, `ns3_downlink_lut.csv`) has cells N in {4, 8, 16, 24, 31} x payload in {1000, 16896} B; `_bracket` clamps below 1000 B, so object sharing (96 + 48 n, about 430 B) is served by the 1000 B cell; late fusion samples the LUT only on the uplink and only when `use_ns3_lut` is set, which no yaml does (default False), and the envelope matrix ran on the hybrid model (SEE-V2X trace RTT plus lognormal backhaul). No SenSys landing run sampled an object-list-sized ns-3 payload; the paper's "ns-3 cosimulation of the C-V2X link" sentence describes the LUT-and-trace model and should say so.

## 2026-10-13 (night): why a late-fusion run took 3 minutes, and the fix
- Profile (`ECAV_PROFILE=1 test_runner.py ...`, cProfile into the run dir; cetus,
  N=1, late_fusion, SBA on, 100 ms): 92 s wall, 178 edge steps at 278 ms. The
  edge step is `_advance_actors` calling `update_info` on the vehicle and both
  RSUs, so one step is three `perception_manager.detect` calls at 90 ms each.
  Inside one detect call: YOLO 22 ms; `project_lidar_to_camera` 25 ms (a Python
  loop painting every projected lidar point onto the image, visualization
  only); `np.array(camera.image)` copies 17 ms; `o3d_camera_lidar_fusion` 9 ms;
  SORT 6 ms; `logger.debug("...%s" % yolo_detection)` and the RSU prints 7 ms
  (eager string formatting of the Detections object and tensors). April's
  per-vehicle perception was 43 ms and its edge step 25 ms because the
  vehicle updates were timed outside the edge step then.
- Fix (3789ca3a): the lidar painting runs only when the camera window is on
  (`draw=self.camera_visualize`), no second image copy, lazy logging arguments,
  RSU prints removed. Outputs are unchanged (the projected points are computed
  before the painting; nothing read the painted image or the strings).
  After: perception 62 ms per call, N=1 run 84 s wall end to end on cetus,
  N=4 174 s (edge step 458 ms = six detect calls). Second round (5bd2338a):
  the camera callback stores a contiguous 3-channel frame (cvtColor was
  copying a strided view, 8 ms per call) and the lidar-to-world transform is
  computed once per detect call (`lidar_points_to_world`) instead of once per
  camera. Projection output checked bit-identical against the old path on a
  20,000-point cloud (scratchpad proj_equiv.py on cetus). Next lever if N=4
  must go faster: one YOLO forward for all actors' cameras per tick instead of
  one per actor (six forwards of 22 ms).
- `scripts/sensys_analysis/campaign_check.py <stamp>`: integrity gates
  (error-path files, runs under 100 frames, missing per-tick CSV, edge frame
  time), per-cell P(S_op) with Wilson intervals next to the April cell, shape

  contract on; G3 P does not rise with latency; G4 SBA beats naive somewhere;
  G5 oracle holds at 200 ms), and the list of cells whose interval straddles
  0.8 with the resume command that adds seeds. Exit 1 on FAIL.
- `scripts/sensys_campaign.sh <role> <stage>`: gate (240 runs per host, same
  cells on both hosts so the hosts are checked against each other), envelope,
  scaling, situation, mixed, faults. The gate stage runs campaign_check and
  stops on FAIL.

### 2026-10-14: the east-approach CAV's 2.5 m lateral drift is a localizer defect (heading wrap), fixed offline

Diagnosis from the defects_fix runs (no CARLA): the global route for the lead
east CAV is on road 24 lane 1 all the way (offline GRP trace, both the old
and the new destination); the local planner's path is that lane centre
(`[TRAJ] mean_k=0.000000`, regenerated every tick because sample_num 10 <
trajectory_update_freq 15, same for every vehicle); the lateral PID is a
heading-to-target controller on trajectory point 1 (about 0.4 s ahead).
What differs is the pose the planner and controller receive: the localizer
hands them the Kalman-filtered (x, y) with the true yaw. The per-vehicle
localization block of simulation_metrics.json shows
filter_yaw_error_mean_deg 264 / 205 / 155 for the drifting east CAV (LTAP
attempt 3 / attempt 2 / SCP 8-ego), 33 for the slower east follower, 112 for
the westbound blind-overtake focal, 195 for the mixed smoke's east CAV, and
0.3 to 3.8 for every vehicle heading north or south; the filtered position
error of the drifting CAV is 0.5 to 1.0 m (x) and 0.7 to 1.3 m (y) against
0.04 to 0.4 m for the others, with the raw GNSS error 0.13 m for all. Cause:
`kalman_filter.run_step` takes the GNSS heading (CARLA yaw in (-180, 180]
plus 1 deg noise) and computes the innovation `z - zPred` without wrapping,
so a westbound vehicle alternates +pi and -pi measurements, the yaw state
settles at a wrong angle (replay: -30, -134, +50 deg for three seeds), and
the motion model (`dt * v * cos/sin(yaw)`) then carries a speed-proportional
position bias that the GNSS update only partly removes (replay at 13.9 m/s:
up to 2.8 m lateral and 7 m longitudinal; at 7.8 m/s: 1.0 m lateral). The
controller steers the biased estimate onto the lane centre, so the true
vehicle runs parallel to the lane, offset by minus the bias: 2.5 m left
at 47 km/h for the lead CAV, 0.3 m for the follower at 28 km/h, nothing for
north/south headings, and the offset appears as the vehicle gains speed
(x = -33). The `[LOC]` line prints raw GNSS error only and hid this.

Fix (commit on the branch): wrap the heading innovation to [-pi, pi) and
normalise the yaw state after the update in
`ecav/core/sensing/localization/kalman_filter.py`; wrap the yaw differences
in `localization_metrics.get_metrics` (the 264 deg figures were themselves
unwrapped). `tests/test_kalman_heading_wrap.py` replays the filter on
synthetic westbound motion: yaw error 0.8 to 1.1 deg and position error
0.05 to 0.08 m for seeds 1 to 3 at 13.9 and 7.8 m/s, equal to northbound
(before: wrong yaw and up to 2.8 m bias). No pytest in opencda310; the file
runs standalone.

Closed-loop verification, to run when the GPU is free (not launched): the
two defects_fix campaigns again with `--stamp kf_wrap` (same flags, port
2200, Town03 preloaded), then check (1) every vehicle's
`localization.filter_yaw_error_mean_deg` under 3 and
`filter_y_error_mean_m` under 0.2, (2) the lead east CAV's GT lateral
offset from the road 24 lane 1 centre within 0.5 m from x = -33 to x = -80
(scratchpad lane-offset script, was +2.5 m), (3) the LTAP 4-ego hero
completing its left turn instead of waiting behind the east CAV, (4) one
`blind_overtake_edge_late_fusion` run with the focal's yaw error under 3
(was 112). overtake_allowed false for the east CAVs (53ce165b) stays: it
was not the cause, but it keeps them from passing the Tesla on the hero's
turn lane.

  contained the literal driver name that the pgrep pattern matched, so pgrep

  patterns and nothing else in that command mentioning the target, then kill by

### 2026-10-14: gate run_4 off-road veer is a zero-lookahead restart in the local planner, fixed offline

Run: experiment_results/openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion/sensys_nov27_gate1/
.../lat_0_..._ego_1_sidr_1.0/run_4 (hero only, 0 ms, SBA on, 70 km/h).
Sequence from the [LOC] GT trace, the per-tick age CSV and the planner
warnings (LOC tick = CSV tick - 48): left turn completed on the arc with
the path 1.7 to 2.0 m to the left of the vehicle (corner cut outside);
tick 159 `[RSS] Enter proper response TTC=1.16s threat_cid=-1` (an
unanchored edge track) while leaving the junction at 46 km/h; decision
brake, brake 1.0, from CSV tick 204 to 224; full stop at (-62.5, 136.4) at
tick 177, 1.0 m right of the eastbound lane centre (135.4), `[RSS] Exit:
ego stopped`; go with throttle 1.0 from tick 178; the hero crept for 14
ticks turning left, then accelerated to 45 km/h while its heading went
-32 (tick 200), -63 (212), -90 (222), -135 deg (228), crossed the westbound
and parking lanes and hit a building at (-54.9, 120.9); Lane Invasion
warnings at ticks 174 and 200; no brake attribution, no planner exception.

What it was following (offline replay of the real LocalPlanner on the
Town03 OpenDRIVE along the GT trace, scratchpad emulate_lp_run4.py): the
global route is 24 waypoints on lane -1 throughout, road 4 -> 291 -> 263
(the turn) -> road 24, no lane-change option; the overtake cannot run
there (the obstacle waypoint's left marking is SolidSolid with lane_change
NONE, the right lane is Parking); get_push_destination from the
junction-exit waypoint returns a point 10 to 13 m ahead on the same lane,
so even a push keeps the lane; the heading-wrap localizer defect does not
apply (headings 90 and 0 deg; filter yaw error 8.7 deg). The defect is the
lateral target itself: `LocalPlanner.run_step` took trajectory point 1,
and `generate_trajectory` spaces points by the motion predicted per
trajectory_dt (0.2 s), so at standstill point 1 is 0.17 m from the path
start. With the vehicle 1 m off centre the heading-error controller saw
an 81 deg error (0.75 * 1.41 rad = 1.06, clipped to the 0.3 steering
limit): full left lock from the first tick of the restart. On tick 177 the
turn's history waypoints were still in the spline (potential_curved_road),
whose start is anchored to the first history node by straight-line
distance, so the path began 1.9 m behind the vehicle and the target angle
was 153 deg. Once the hero swung past the centre line the target stayed
abeam or behind it (path start up to 14 m behind by tick 227), the
acos-based error stayed saturated, and at the normal 47 km/h target speed
it spiralled off the road. Why 1 in 60: a scan of all 129 gate1 runs finds
exactly one standstill restart on the eastbound segment after the turn
(run_4); every other stop was on the approach, where a restart aims
straight down the lane with a near-zero offset.

Fix (commit 1e11f96a): the lateral target is the first trajectory point
at least max(2.5 m, 0.4 s * v) ahead of the vehicle along its heading; if
the whole sampled trajectory is abeam or behind, the first route waypoint
ahead; else the last trajectory point. At 47 km/h this is the same second
sample as before (replay: 5.3 m ahead). tests/test_local_planner_lookahead.py
replays the run_4 stop on the real planner: target 2.67 m ahead at -22 deg
(was 0.17 m at -81 deg; -153 deg with the history-anchored start), stops at
x -60/-55/-50 give 2.6 m at -21 to -26 deg, moving 47 km/h unchanged.
Not touched: the straight-line `diff_s` start of the spline (the fallback
covers it) and the RSS trigger (the unanchored threat is the paper's
phenomenon).

Closed-loop verification when the GPU is free (not launched): the gate cell
that produced it, `python test_runner.py -t openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion
--manager-types late_fusion --anchoring on --latencies 0 --speeds 70
--ego-counts 1 --repetitions 10 --self-id-radius 1.0 --carla-port 2200
--stamp lookahead_check`, then the LTAP 4-ego and SCP 8-ego defects_fix
runs again: no off-road or static collision, the hero reaches its
destination or MAX_STEP, and in the GT trace no heading change above 30 deg
within 2 s of any standstill restart (restart_scan.py in the scratchpad
does this check on a results tree).
- 15:45: local planner lookahead fix merged (1e11f96a: the lateral target is the
  first trajectory point at least max(2.5 m, 0.4 s x speed) ahead; a standstill

### 2026-10-14: cross-traffic track loss at the RSU handover is an association defect, fixed offline (branch sensys/edge-track-handover)

Runs: sensys_nov27_gate3_partial anchoring_on lat_0 run_4 (hero collided
with the Tesla) and sensys_nov27_gate1 lat_0 run_10, late-fusion edge,
AB3DMOT (det_name pvrcnn: hungar, dist_2d 4 m, min_hits 3, max_age 6).
Ground truth: every per_tick_age.csv row of a tick carries conflict_dist_m
against the same live GT point, so three or more rows trilaterate the
Tesla per tick (residual 0.00; scratchpad gt_trilat.py, now inside
scripts/diag/replay_edge_tracker.py). The Tesla (actor 455, WaypointFollower
at 13.4 m/s) starts at tick 26, accelerates 2.8 to 13.7 m/s by tick 60
(the "5 m/s" of track 29 over ticks 31 to 63 is half real: GT was 4.6 to
13.7 m/s there, the KF lagged by 3 to 7 m/s), holds 13 m/s, crosses the
conflict point (-84.8) at tick 113. The published conflict-actor track was
absent for ticks 64 to 65, 69 to 74, 76 to 81 and 104 to 119, the last gap
covering the crossing.

Why the track dies. Not detection: both RSUs report the Tesla on every
tick from 26 to 97, rsu_-2 alone from 98 to 120 (rsu_-1 at (-82, 126) loses
it inside 8 m), the hero's own camera from 109. The two RSUs see different
faces: the fusion box sits at the nearest-surface centroid
(o3d_lidar_libs._nearest_surface_centroid, mean of the nearest half of the
points), so rsu_-1, looking at the front, reports 0.7 m ahead of the GT
centre and rsu_-2, looking at the rear plus its 2D SORT lag, 2.5 m behind:
3.3 m apart on average, 4.5 m worst case, 68 percent of ticks at 3 m or
more. rsu_-2 also repeats a stale box on 20 of 94 ticks (the perception
step reuses the last camera image). The edge's _cross_source_nms (3 m,
keeps the first-listed source) let the pair through on those ticks, and
AB3DMOT's own nms() merged it within max(l, w) but keeps the LAST-listed of
equal scores (argsort(scores)[::-1]), so the measurement handed to the KF
flipped between the front face and the rear face by 3 to 4 m. The
kinematic innovation gate in AB3DMOT_libs/matching.py then rejected it:
kf_speed_ground is the KF state velocity per tracker frame (m/tick, one
frame per source tick, see _ab3d_history_to_trajs dividing by dt) but the
gate compared it with m/s constants, so every track below 10 m/s counted
as stationary with a 1.0 m gate and a 13 m/s track got max(0.65 * 0.05 +
1.0, 1.5) = 1.5 m. The rejected track coasts (output() zeroes the
published velocity while time_since_update > 0, so the planner's linear
predictor emits a stationary prediction), dies after max_age 6, and the
unmatched detections birth a new id, which the predictor ignores until it
has been published in 10 of the last 30 frames
(linear_predictor_manager._MIN_HISTORY_ANONYMOUS). Each re-birth therefore
costs 13 ticks of planner blindness; run_4 went through tracks 29, 48, 56,
60, 63, 81, 84, 93 in 90 ticks. The jitter buffer also fed 8 of 599 frames
out of order (a later packet arriving first; drain() sorts only what is
ready), a 0.65 m backward innovation each time; secondary, not changed.

Why the tracked speed is low. Three parts: the Tesla really was slow
until tick 51 (GT 4.6 to 11 m/s over the life of track 29); the KF
(R = 3, Q_vel = 0.01) lags an accelerating target by 3 to 7 m/s; and every
published zero is a coasting frame, not a tracker estimate. Detections are
not late (gen_tick = publish_tick at 0 ms). KF velocity initialisation is
not the issue: P_vel = 1000 makes the second update set the velocity from
the displacement; the phantom 16 to 49 m/s of newborn tracks in the replay
comes from the face flip inside their first three frames.

Fix (smallest set that holds the track through the handover, applied in
the shared tracker and the shared NMS so every arm gets it: naive, SBA,
ETSI, I2V and CIP inherit _collect_detections_for_frame from
PredictionLateFusionEdge; VIPS calls _cross_source_nms itself; oracle has
no NMS but shares matching.py):
1. matching.py: trk_speed = kf_speed_ground / _DT before the gate, so the
   stationary rule applies below 0.5 m/s as its comment says and the speed
   term is the real per-tick displacement.
2. matching.py: _D_BASE 1.0 to 3.0 m, the measured cross-view disagreement;
   the dist_2d threshold (4 m) still bounds the innovation above it. The
   stationary gate (1.0 m) is unchanged, so the parked-car hijack the gate
   was built for is still rejected.
3. _cross_source_nms default 3.0 to 5.0 m (one car length, the same radius
   perception_manager's cross-camera NMS uses), both call sites on the
   default, so one face per vehicle per frame reaches the tracker; the
   copy in fusion/late_fusion_backend.py (adaptive and SOTA pluggable
   edges) set to the same value.
Not changed: max_age (longer coasting publishes a stationary ghost: with
max_age 12 alone 46 percent of planner-visible ticks were stationary
predictions and 36 ticks coasted at a 12.3 m/s speed error), the KF
noise, the centroid itself, time_since_update semantics (a re-association
is a real measurement update, so obs_tick = source_tick -
time_since_update stays the observation time).

Offline verification (scripts/diag/replay_edge_tracker.py: rebuilds every
tracker frame from the [DET] lines in drain order, drives the real AB3DMOT
with the edge's mot_cfg and the edge's NMS, scores against the
trilaterated GT over ticks 26 to 136; before the change it reproduces the
logged tracks, same ids and positions to 0.1 m through tick 63). Mean of
run_4 and run_10:
| setting | ids | tracker gap | published v err | coasting ticks (v err) | planner-visible uncovered / max gap | stationary frac |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 12.5 | 2 | 6.9 m/s | 27 (12.5 m/s) | 58.5 / 44.5 | 0.18 |
| unit fix only | 9.5 | 1 | 6.3 | 23.5 (12.4) | 43 / 25.5 | 0.21 |
| unit fix + 3 m allowance | 3 | 0 | 3.5 | 11.5 (11.6) | 7.5 / 7.5 | 0.07 |
| + 5 m NMS (shipped) | 1 | 0 | 2.2 | 0.5 | 4 / 4 | 0.01 |
| max_age 12 alone | 7.5 | 1.5 | 6.7 | 36 (12.3) | 14.5 / 10.5 | 0.46 |
Allowance sweep with the unit fix and 5 m NMS: 2.0 m gives 3.5 ids,
2.5 m 2.5, 3.0 m 1. The shipped result is identical at both extent
extremes the log lacks (3.5 and 5.5 m boxes) and with anchoring off. After
the fix the Tesla is track 23 from its parked state to tick 136 with a

switch (rsu_-2's rear-face box is 2.5 m behind), back to 12.9 m/s by tick

All 212 complete lat_0 to lat_500 runs of gate1 and gate3_partial,

The per-latency rows (0 to 500 ms) all move the same way (ids 8 to 12

  (kmax 0.124 to 0.033, limit 23 to 45 km/h); it exits at y = 137.6, 2.2 m
  right of the road 24 lane centre (135.4), heading -20 deg, and is back on
  the centre by x = -65 with a +5 to +14 deg correction (steer +0.08 to
  +0.22). Every diag run that completed (5 of 6; run_4 lost its metrics to a
  PyGILState crash at cleanup after reaching the destination) shows the
  same two re-plans and the same wide exit.
- The drifting policy_smoke run is the same sequence with a slower hero
  (ttc_graded held it at 14 to 26 km/h in the arc, which keeps it longer
  inside the junction overlap zone): along the exit the nearest Driving lane
  flips between 263/-1 and the overlapping junction lanes 239/-1 (yaw -42),
  316/1 (179), 282/-1 (-86), 350/1 (160 to 173), 271/-1 (-85), 255/1 (179),
  whose centres pass within 0.3 to 1.0 m of the hero's lane (lane_probe.py
  on the GT trace). A push (the 90-tick hold from the entry push had
  expired) or the reset after it, taken from 316/1, 350/1 or 255/1, routes
  the hero 513 m around the block: first waypoints (-72.2, 129.3), (-73.8,
  126.0), (-74.0, 120.4) (grp_probe.py). From 282/-1 it is 380 m south
  along x = -77.5. The spline from the eastbound history nodes onto that
  route carries the 0.2 kink (18 km/h limit, the crawl), and the target
  selection (first trajectory point 2.5 m ahead, else last point) steers
  the hero left onto it: heading -11, -27, -37, -56, -63 deg from x = -73 to
  -66, into the parking lane and the pole.

So the coordinator's candidate (hold the curvature-limited speed until the
heading error is small, or for a fixed distance past the arc) does not
remove it: in the failing run the hero was already at 8 to 18 km/h through
the exit. The spline start offset at speed is not the cause either: in the
instrumented runs the path start stays within 0.1 to 1.5 m ahead of the
vehicle; the 2 to 3 m lateral offset through the arc is the vehicle wide of
the path after the pushed overshoot.

Fix (behavior_agent.py):
1. `check_lane_change_permission` records `lane_change_blocked`, True only
   when a planned lane change (lane id and lateral change on the route) is
   refused by the adjacent-lane collision check; the push case keys on it
   instead of on `lane_change_allowed`. A sharp turn no longer pushes the
   destination.
2. `route_start_waypoint(map, location, ego_yaw, route_waypoints)`: the
   nearest lane is used as the route start only when its direction is
   within 60 deg of the heading; otherwise the first route waypoint still
   ahead and aligned; else the nearest lane. Used by `set_destination`
   (push, reset, overtake re-plans), computed before the buffers are
   cleared. Test tests/test_route_start_lane.py: at (-80.6, 132.3) yaw 33
   the nearest lane is 316/1 (yaw 179) and the start becomes 263/-1 2.6 m
   ahead; same for 350/1 and 255/1 positions; the route from the chosen
   start is under 60 m (the nearest-lane route was 513 m); the nearest lane
   is kept on road 24; no heading or no route waypoints fall back to the
   nearest lane.

## 2026-10-16 16:40: junction hero stall root-caused, overtake horizon root-caused, fixes in b8639d1c, tests running

Margin probes stopped on both hosts (atlas scenario_3 at 60 m run 10 of 30, cetus SCP at 45 m run 17 of 30; YAMLs restored from .bak). Two reasons. The hero's straight approach never comes within 49.8 m of the crossing car's spawn (-35, 127.7), so the 45 and 30 m trigger cells can never launch it. The hero's own approach is not seed-invariant (below), so the crossing phasing is random at any trigger distance.

Junction stall, root cause (diag run stamp diag_column, oracle 70 km/h 0 ms, 3 seeds, BEHAVIOR_DEBUG=1, plus the passive actor tap):
- The scenario in use is scenario_3_occluded.xml: five static firetrucks at x=-81, y=83.7, 92.7, 101.7, 110.7, 119.7 (not the five cars in scenario_3.xml). The oracle's valid-type list excludes firetruck, so the oracle publishes no ground-truth track for them; the tracks at the truck ends (y 96.9, 106.8) and the moving anonymous tracks at (-82, 85 to 93) come from the hero's own perception uplink. [LP]/[TRAJ]/[CTL] log speeds are km/h; the per-tick CSV ego_speed_mps is m/s.
- In every seed the hero launches at tick 24 and gets a target speed of 0 at tick 33 to 39 ([TRAJ] target_before=0.0). The path: branch 5c "in-path stationary lead during approach" (73944a1f, 2026-08-16) calls _find_blocking_lead, whose local-object loop (8de40397, 2026-08-05) accepted a perceived column box at ahead 23 m, lateral 1.6 to 1.7 m (gate 1.75 m since 020a4bbc), so car_following_manager returned 0 for a stopped lead. Ground truth: the hero decelerates from 7.4 to 0 m/s between y=83.7 and 85.5 and sits there 1 to 5 s depending on seed (seven of ten seeds in curv8_probe), then re-accelerates. No HAZARD or STOP line is logged on this path.
- The crossing car launches at tick 0 (the 80 m trigger is wider than the 69 m spawn separation) and occupies the hero's lane at ticks 107 to 115 in every seed. Seeds where the hero arrives in time yield with a full stop from about 20 m (oracle, 0 ms); the margin diagnostic (scripts/diag/junction_margin.py) shows the hero reaching the crossing car's lane 16 to 112 ticks after it cleared. That is why the oracle held to 1,000 ms and beyond.

Overtake, root cause (overtake_gate43, oracle 43 km/h 0 ms with ONCOMING_SPEED=12 TRIGGER_DIST=300: 2 of 10, 8 collisions): the single RSU sits at (295, 200) with 50 m sensing, so the first oncoming car enters the edge's view at x of about 245, 3 s before the truck. The launch rule needs the nearest oncoming at least 4 s x (7 + v_onc) = 76 m away and treats no oncoming as clear, so the hero launched at tick 65 with the oncoming 47 m out and unpublished, and met it head-on at x of about 299. Khonsu's warm arm saw the oncoming through the locale_1 handoff (its RSU2 at x=180); Khonsu's own table has the cold arm at 0 of 10 at 12 m/s. The SenSys single-RSU overtake was Khonsu's cold arm.

Fixes, commit b8639d1c (both hosts):
- behavior_agent.py: branch 5c runs only when the YAML allows overtaking (overtake_allowed_origin); openscenario_3 and scp YAMLs set overtake_allowed false.
- scenario_3.py: CROSS_TRIGGER_TTA (seconds) launches the crossing car when the hero's time to arrival at the conflict point (-84.8, 127.9) drops below the value (InTimeToArrivalToLocation); the distance trigger stays the default. This is the knob for the speed study: the distance trigger fires at a fixed hero position, so the crossing phasing changed with approach speed.

## 2026-10-17 08:55: brake-label defect found and corrected post hoc (bb6153b5, 3b9b299c)

The contract arm at 88 km/h read 0.00 at 0 ms with 16 "false brake" episodes while every brake trigger sat at the crossing car (anonymous track at (-53 to -59, 128)). Cause: the run-time labeller's track provenance tags a frame 'ego' when the nearest actor in the edge's range-limited ground-truth snapshot is a managed CAV; a crossing car first seen beyond that range (the hero at 88 km/h brakes at TTC 2.4 s, 58 m out) has no snapshot entry, the nearest remaining actor is the hero itself, the track's provenance becomes 'self_ghost', and the class is set from provenance although the labeller's own full-world match found the crossing car at 0.4 to 1.6 m (gt_matched_actor_id = the car). recompute's reclassification then turned those "self_ghost" labels into other_fp (not in the ego corridor) and S_op failed. The same mechanism produced one mislabelled brake per run in the 70 km/h cells (the 0.80 to 0.90 at 0 to 300 ms of naive, ETSI and contract in the gate tables above) and at 38 and 53.

Fix (analysis code only, no rerun): recompute relabels a self_ghost attribution whose GT match is a non-ego actor within 3 m by the match: the run's conflict actor (per-tick log conflict_actor_id) gives true_positive, any other actor other_fp. Corrected cells (10 seeds per host): 70 km/h naive 1.00, 1.00, then 0.00 from 200 on both hosts; ETSI 1.00, 0.90 (atlas) and 1.00, 1.00 (cetus) then 0.00 from 200; contract 1.00, 1.00, 0.90, 0.90 or 1.00, 0.10 or 0.00, 0.60 or 0.30; 88 km/h contract 1.00, 1.00, 0.00 at 0, 100, 200; 38 km/h contract 1.00 to 400, 0.80 at 500; naive at 38 0.90, 1.00, 0.90, 0.60, 0.00, 0.00; at 53 0.90, 0.90, 0.90, 0.80, 0.00, 0.00. Remaining sub-1.00 low-delay cells are other_fp brakes to read per cell. The run-time labeller (edge_manager_base, provenance rule) is corrected after the stage ends, not during it (one code version per stage); the recompute rule makes the stage's labels right either way. Every table in this file above 08:55 that shows 0.80 or 0.90 at 0 to 100 ms carries the defect.
campaign_check's age column now comes from the paper's reduction (a628a4a9): the oracle at configured 0 ms reads p50 0 / p99 191 ms (decision window) instead of 1,050; its transition-bracketing list uses the same value. Shipped to cetus.

- Tyler: "You're probably misreading the edge as the edge also runs the vehicle steps." Confirmed. In the late-fusion manager (ecav/core/application/edge/edge_manager/edge_manager_prediction_late_fusion_ab3dmot_linear_predictor.py) the profiler frame opens at line 813 and the step ends with `if not self.run_distributed: self._advance_actors(tick)` at line 1391, inside the frame. `_advance_actors` runs every CAV's `update_info` (YOLO perception), `run_step` (planning) and `apply_control`, the brake-attribution labelling and time-to-event records, the non-member step, both RSUs' `update_info` and `run_step` (RSU perception), and a live ground-truth snapshot for the conflict kinematics log. The scenario loop (openscenario_3_edge_late_fusion.py line 235) calls only `edge.run_step(step)` in the one-process mode the campaign uses, so the vehicles are stepped nowhere else. `timing_avg_ms` is therefore the simulation step on the client side, not the edge.

  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 20 | 104 | 14.2 | 8.5 | 2.7 | 1.9 | 0.4 | 27 | 3 | 13.0 |

  CAV perception is about 30 ms per CAV, sequential on the one GPU (that is the 50 ms per agent together with planning). Edge compute grows with detections per frame (tracking dominates: AB3DMOT association over 13 to 31 detections). ### 2026-10-19 14:00: faults stage collision mechanisms traced as far as the records allow

- The collision sensor callback (`_count_collisions`, vehicle_manager.py line 525) counts events and does not record the other actor, so the partner is inferred: a managed CAV when that CAV's own collision count is also non-zero in the same run (CAV-CAV), otherwise a non-managed actor (the crossing car or a static object). Instrumentation to add after the atlas chains end (no behaviour change): store event.other_actor id and type per collision in the metrics.
- Position noise 0.5 m, LT contract (5 of 5 collisions, no other CAV collided): in every seed the last brakes are at ticks 249 to 251 on the static object at (-65.8, 134.7) beside the junction exit lane (the "beside-lane static false positive" of the N=4 phantom class; it is a parked vehicle) with the hero at 12.2 m/s and TTC 0.5 s, and the collision follows within two ticks. In the no-fault cell the hero reaches the same spot at 8.3 m/s (brakes at 14 m, TTC 1.7 s, no collision) because it stopped at the junction entrance for the crossing car at ticks 240 to 260; with the noisy beacon it stopped once at tick 200 and then accelerated through the junction to 12 m/s. The fault changes the hero's junction timing through the tracks it consumes (its own anchored track moves by the noise), and the parked vehicle at the exit turns from a phantom brake into a collision at the higher exit speed. The collision partner is inferred from the brake geometry and the absence of a managed partner.
- ValidBeacon under delay: SCP contract vb delay 2 (4 of 5) and delay 4 (5 of 5) are CAV-CAV collisions (another managed CAV's count is non-zero in the same run). At delay 2 the hero brakes at tick 157 at 13.2 m/s inside the junction for an anonymous track at its own position (TTC 0.0): the delayed beacon is rejected by the validity checks, the hero's own echo loses its anchor and returns as an anonymous track on top of the hero, the planner emergency-brakes mid-junction and a connected vehicle strikes it. At delay 4 the last brakes are on crossing managed CAVs at 17 to 18 m/s with TTC 1.7 to 1.9 s. On the left turn (vb delay 1, 4 of 5) the last brakes are on the parked vehicle at 5 to 6 m/s with TTC 2 to 3 s and no managed partner, so the partner there is a non-managed actor; not resolved further.
- Loss 0.5, LT contract without checks (5 of 5): three seeds end with brakes on cav3 (the westbound crosser) at 1.9 m/s at the junction entrance, no managed partner, so the hero is struck by the non-managed crossing car while crawling; two seeds end on the parked vehicle. Not resolved further without the partner record.
- Consequence for the faults figure: the contract's tolerance to beacon delay (through 4 ticks, both geometries) and the self-ghost return at 8 ticks are clean identity results; the ValidBeacon harm under delay is a real mechanism (rejected beacon = lost anchor = own echo as an anonymous hazard); the position-noise and loss collisions on the left turn run through the junction-exit parked vehicle and the crossing-car timing, which are layout properties of the N=4 left turn, and the figure should report the collision class with that note rather than as an identity effect.

- 22:35: the junction inversion is now verified on the planner's own inputs (scratchpad replay_trace.py, replay_margin.py). Replaying the logged path and forecast at each run's first flagged tick reproduces both flags exactly (oracle TTC 0.95 at hero y 111.8; contract TTC 1.45 at y 104.8). With the oracle's exact state moved back along the approach, the time-synchronised miss distance declines slowly: 2.3 m at y 99.8, 2.2 m at 103.8 to 104.8, 2.1 at 105.8, 2.0 at 106.8 to 107.8, 1.9 at 108.8 to 109.8, 1.8 at 110.8 to 111.8, so the check's 2 m threshold is reached with exact state about 20 m from the conflict, which at 18.3 m/s is too late to stop. The contract's consumed state at y 104.8 gives a 1.8 m miss where the exact state gives 2.2: its forecast carries a lateral component (y 127.8 to 129.7 over the 3 s horizon, 0.6 m/s toward the hero's exit side) and a slightly lower speed (12.8 against 13.2 m/s); cross-substitution shows the lateral drift is what shaves the 0.4 m (the contract's path with the oracle's forecast and speed still flags, with the oracle's forecast and the contract's speed does not, with the contract's forecast and either speed does). So the camera-lidar arms cross the planner's hazard threshold about 7 m earlier in the approach than exact state does, because their forecast of a car seen from two masts carries a small lateral velocity toward the hero's path; at 400 ms the exact state reaches the threshold early enough and the oracle passes. For the paper: the oracle row is the exact-state reference; at the boundary a forecast bias of a few tenths of a metre toward the hero's path moves the hazard one delay step earlier, and the arms' advantage there is that bias, not information.

- Reading. On the straight crossing the graded deceleration (target speed = max speed x TTC / 3 s, emergency stop as fallback) does not stop the hero before the conflict at 70 or 88 km/h even with exact zero-age state: the policy itself lies below the maneuver's physics, so the useful-age budget under it is zero, against 300 ms (70 km/h) and 200 ms (88) under the stop policy. The isolated 1.00 at 70 km/h and 300 ms is one trajectory repeated ten times (deterministic per configuration) in which the delayed state makes the hero brake at a moment that clears the car. On the left turn the same policy kept the budget and changed only the failure mix. Panel (c) therefore shows the controller dependence as geometry-specific: the budget is a property of the maneuver and the controller together, which is the claim the reviewer asked to see tested. The mechanism trace (speed at the last brake, TTC) is below.
- The contract sweep (1.5 / 2 / 3 s at the five censored low-speed cells, 150 runs) started 22:34 on cetus.
- Trace (SCP 70 km/h, graded, 0 ms, identical in every seed): six true-positive brakes on the crossing car at TTC 2.65 s (57 m, hero 17.8 m/s), 1.30 s (31 m, 19.9 m/s: the hero has accelerated, since the graded target at TTC 2.65 s is 0.88 of max speed) and 0.30 s (7 m, 19.5 m/s), then the collision at 179 frames; mean speed 16 m/s through the junction. The graded target (max speed x TTC / 3 s) only drops below a stopping speed when TTC is under about 1 s, by which point stopping from 19 m/s is impossible, so the policy is unsafe on the straight crossing whatever the age. At 300 ms (the 1.00 cell) the delayed state moves the brakes to TTC 0.9 to 0.25 s at 16.5 m/s and the car has passed when the hero reaches the conflict point: one trajectory repeated ten times, not tolerance. On the left turn the hero approaches at about 10 m/s and the same policy stops in time. For the paper: the useful-age budget is a property of the maneuver and the controller together; under the graded policy it is 300 and 200 ms on the left turn (as under the stop policy) and zero on the straight crossing.

The in-order replay cells on the j3 code: contract L 0/10, M 7/10, H 8/10; naive 0/10 on all three; every failure a collision. Mechanism (replay-L contract run_1): conflict-actor age p50 50 ms, p99 200 ms, max 300 ms, but coverage 0.69 with a 30-tick (1.5 s) gap between consecutive conflict-actor rows: the replay turns recorded delivery gaps into bursts of dropped messages (up to 20 per gap, shared by every sender through one latency model), the planner holds no state for the car across the burst and collides at a low p99 age. The trace's own period is 20 ms at every intersection (median inter-arrival 20.0 ms; gaps above 30 ms are 2 to 32 percent of messages by sender, most on t1/t2 at intersections 4 and 5), so the replay_period_ms=20 assumption is right. Consequence for 5.2.5 as written ("replay cells fall inside the envelope's interval"): on the j3 code a scalar p99 does not predict these cells; envelope_predict.py's coverage and gap predictors are the test to report, and the text must say which predictor holds. The planner fix (hold cache plus re-indexing) extrapolates a held forecast across a burst, so j4 may move these cells; pilot does not cover them. Also found: the pooled envelope figure's zero-delay points had absorbed the replay cells (same knobs); runs.csv now carries the cell name and the builders skip v2x_regime rows; reducer rerunning (pid 1827331).

Exact-state reference passes 10/10 at every delay to 700 ms and 9/10 at 1,000 ms on both geometries (j3: 475 and 525 ms budgets). Contract arm 10/10 to 400 ms and 0/10 at 500 ms on both (LT: 8 collisions; SCP: 10 "other fp"). Naive arm 10/10 to 400 on LT with NO self-ghost at any delay (j3: 20 to 40 episodes per cell from 375 ms); on SCP naive ghosts 8/10 at 500 ms (genuine, ego copy 5.8 m behind at 4.5 m/s after the yield). N=4 LT (5 seeds): naive 5/5, 4/5, 5/5 at 100/200/400, no ghost. Read-only diagnosis (fork, 11:55 to 12:05): (1) LT contract 500 ms collisions are physics class from the tracker's velocity estimate of the launching crossing car: late-fusion track 9.3 m/s where the oracle reports 11.7 at the same car position, the estimate oscillates 9.3 to 13.0 over obs ticks 112 to 128 while the truth climbs 12 to 13.5 (car at ~7 m/s2 from rest), YOLO frames consumed 12 to 16 of 20 ticks; re-indexing shifts the forecast origin by v_est x age so the forecast falls 4 to 7 m short at 1.5 to 2 s lookahead (above the 2.5 m margin); collision=True only at TTC 1.2 s, 17 m from the conflict, stopping needs ~22 m. Code path: AB3DMOT CV filter on intermittent detections -> forecast_age re-indexing -> collision_check 2.5 m. (2) SCP contract 500 ms "fp" brakes are ALL brakes on the crossing car (gt id = conflict actor, d 7.9 m, TTC 2.1 s, ego yields and completes): the post-hoc labeler's conflict-actor match radius (6 m, recompute_metrics.py _is_conf) is below the stale offset 12.2 m/s x 0.55 s = 7.2 to 7.9 m at 500 ms, so it falls through to other_fp/beside_lane. Same artifact in the LT 500 "fp" runs and likely the SCP 400 fp. Reduction defect, no rerun needed; the fix is to match the braking track by its GT actor id (already in the brake record) or scale the radius with v x age. (3) LT naive copies are still published and consumed (track 0 = ego cid, 170 rows in run_1) but re-indexing moves the copy's forecast start to median 2.9 m from the ego (j3: 8.0 to 8.7 m), inside the planner's 5 m single-nearest self-suppression (behavior_agent.py:982-1011, anchoring off only), so the copy is the suppressed track; the ghost survives when another track is nearer (SCP tick 201: parked car at 3.57 m beats the copy at 3.79 m, the parked car gets suppressed and the copy brakes). IMPLICATIONS: "contract within one bin of the reference" fails at 70 km/h (400 vs >=1,000 ms) because of perception velocity error under age, not identity; the naive arm's early logic failure vanishes at N=1 and N=4 on LT 70; the logic-failure evidence rests on SCP (and whatever N=4/88 km/h show). Tyler's call: accept and reframe (V2X arms have a perception-limited budget below the exact-state reference) or fix the tracker's velocity lag (process noise / CA model) and restart j4.
